title: Blume: Zero-Config Docs Framework That Turns a Markdown Folder into an AI-Ready Website
gist: Hayden Bleasel open-sourced Blume, a zero-config Markdown-to-docs-site framework built on Astro and Vite that ships llms.txt, raw Markdown endpoints, and an MCP server for agent readability plus a 'blume eval' CI check that fails builds when an AI agent can't answer questions from the docs, positioning itself as a middle ground between hosted Mintlify and library-based rivals like Docusaurus and Fumadocs.

themes.theme: Zero-config architecture: the framework is the template

insights.claim: Blume is a zero-config documentation framework, released as open source by Hayden Bleasel, that renders a folder of Markdown into a complete docs site with automatic SEO and AEO, 30+ components, and no app boilerplate to write.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Removing boilerplate and app scaffolding lowers the setup cost for teams building docs sites, directly competing with library-based frameworks that require ongoing app maintenance.
insights.quote: a world-class docs framework for everything you ship

insights.claim: Blume's central architectural claim is that the framework itself is the template, so there is nothing to clone: its CLI loads blume.config.ts, scans content into a graph, and generates a hidden Astro project under .blume/ that it drives for dev and build.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: This 'framework as template' model differs from scaffold-then-maintain approaches, reducing long-term maintenance burden since users never own or diverge from the generated app code.
insights.locator: The central claim is that the framework is the template

insights.claim: Blume is built on Astro and Vite, licensed MIT on GitHub, requires only Node.js 22.12 or newer and one Markdown file to run, and is set up via three commands: npx blume init, blume dev, and blume build.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A minimal, three-command setup path with permissive MIT licensing reduces adoption friction for engineering teams evaluating documentation tooling.
insights.locator: Node.js 22.12 or newer and one Markdown file are the only prerequisites

insights.claim: Blume's core theme ships zero client framework JavaScript, and configuration is opt-in and type-safe, validated by a schema through a defineConfig function.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Shipping zero client framework JavaScript by default suggests strong performance characteristics out of the box, a selling point versus React-runtime-based docs frameworks.
insights.locator: a core theme that ships zero client framework JavaScript

insights.claim: Blume sites automatically emit llms.txt and llms-full.txt files, serve raw Markdown at any .md URL, and can expose a hosted MCP server, making documentation directly consumable by AI agents.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Built-in agent-readability formats (llms.txt, raw Markdown, MCP) position Blume to capture demand from teams optimizing their docs for AI coding assistants and retrieval-augmented tools.

insights.claim: Blume includes a 'blume eval' feature that turns documentation into a test suite: an AI agent answers user questions using only the documentation, a judge model grades the answers, and continuous integration fails when the docs cannot answer.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Treating documentation quality as a CI-gated, agent-graded metric is a novel quality-assurance model that could become a template for other AI-ready documentation tooling.
insights.locator: blume eval turns docs into a test suite

insights.claim: Asked on Product Hunt what 'AI-ready' concretely means, Blume's creator Hayden Bleasel said it covers llms.txt, raw markdown via negotiation headers, MCP servers, agent readability, and skills, all aimed at making docs easier for agents to read.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The creator's own definition clarifies that 'AI-ready' is a bundle of concrete technical mechanisms rather than a marketing label, useful for evaluating competing 'AI-ready docs' claims from other tools.
insights.quote: Means lots of things - llms.txt, raw markdown via negotiation headers, mcp servers, agent readability, skills. All in the pursuit of making your docs easier to read by agents.

themes.theme: Competitive positioning against Mintlify, Docusaurus, Fumadocs, Nextra, Starlight

insights.claim: Blume's own comparison table frames Mintlify as a hosted platform with a closed core, and frames Fumadocs, Nextra, and Docusaurus as a library plus an app that users scaffold and then maintain on a React runtime.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: This framing lets investors and buyers quickly map the docs-tooling competitive landscape into three categories: closed hosted, library-plus-maintained-app, and Blume's claimed open middle ground.
insights.locator: Against rivals, Blume's comparison table frames Mintlify

insights.claim: Blume claims a middle-ground position versus rivals: open source, hostable anywhere, with only Markdown to own, offering escape hatches through component overrides and a 'blume eject' command that promotes the generated runtime into a standalone Astro app.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The eject escape hatch mitigates lock-in risk for adopters, addressing a common objection to opinionated zero-config frameworks.

insights.claim: Blume bundles a blume-migrate skill that converts source configuration from Mintlify, Docusaurus, Fumadocs, Nextra, and Starlight into blume.config.ts, restructures content into filesystem-derived navigation with redirects for every moved route, rewrites callouts to ::: directives, converts icons to Lucide, and points generated API references at openapi.sources.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: An automated migration path from five named competitors directly lowers switching costs, a deliberate strategy to capture existing docs-framework users rather than only greenfield projects.
insights.locator: The changelog describes a bundled blume-migrate skill

insights.claim: A third party, PunGrumpy, published an account of migrating the Logixlysia project's documentation from Fumadocs to Blume.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A real, independently published migration case study is early evidence that the migration tooling works in practice, not just in marketing claims.

insights.claim: On GitHub, user TimonVS requested route-based page tabs for design system docs, noting that using Starlight had forced 'an ugly component override of the PageTitle component,' and Bleasel shipped a query-parameter-based tabs feature within a day.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A same-day feature turnaround from the maintainer suggests high responsiveness that could accelerate community trust and adoption in the early project stage.
insights.quote: an ugly component override of the PageTitle component
insights.locator: On GitHub, TimonVS asked for route-based page tabs

insights.claim: The shipped query-parameter tabs solution covers a shareable tab URL and multiple tab groups per page, but does not yet support a separate indexed URL per tab.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A known SEO/indexing gap (no per-tab indexed URL) is a concrete limitation for teams relying on Blume for content that needs individual tab-level search indexing.
insights.quote: So the query-param version covers "shareable tab URL" and "multiple groups per page," but not "a separate indexed URL per tab."
insights.locator: Bleasel shipped query-parameter tabs within a day

insights.claim: Reported issues in Blume include dark mode elements flickering during client-side navigation and incorrect font fallback rendering for Vietnamese text.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Localization and theming bugs are typical early-stage rough edges that could affect international or accessibility-focused adopters until patched.
insights.locator: Other issues reported dark mode elements flickering

insights.claim: Blume's own FAQ documents that the Markdown formatter oxfmt collapses ':::note' directives onto a single line so they render as literal text, an upstream bug inherited from Prettier's Markdown printer, with a pinned patch offered as a workaround.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The bug's root cause lies upstream in Prettier's Markdown printer rather than in Blume itself, meaning the fix timeline depends partly on an external project.
insights.locator: Blume's own FAQ documents highlighted a formatting issue

insights.claim: Blume passed 1,300 GitHub stars and reached number seven on GitHub's TypeScript trending list.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Rapid star accumulation and a top-ten trending placement are concrete, verifiable early adoption signals for a newly launched open-source project.
insights.locator: it has passed 1,300 stars and reached number seven

insights.claim: Blume ranked second of the day on Product Hunt with 304 upvotes shortly after launch, and MarkTechPost had covered the project in July.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Strong Product Hunt performance plus earlier trade-press coverage indicates building momentum and media interest ahead of the wider open-source release.
insights.locator: Blume ranked second of the day on Product Hunt

insights.claim: Blume is maintained by Hayden Bleasel, an Australian design engineer whose other projects include Ultracite and Files SDK.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The maintainer's existing portfolio of developer tooling projects (Ultracite, Files SDK) suggests a track record that may lend credibility and cross-project distribution for Blume.
insights.locator: maintained by Hayden Bleasel, an Australian design engineer
